title: Airport & Immigration
description: Getting through immigration and customs, finding your bags and your gate, and what to say if a suitcase goes missing or a flight is late. Officers at big airports often speak English, but a few Indonesian answers go down well.

phrases.registerNotes: Ini … saya (here's my …) works for anything you hand over: ini tiket saya (here's my ticket).

phrases.indonesian: Loket visa on arrival di mana, ya?
phrases.english: Where's the visa on arrival counter?
phrases.registerNotes: Loket is a counter or ticket window. Visa on arrival keeps its English name, often written VoA.
phrases.cultureNote: Visitors from New Zealand can usually get a visa on arrival, paid at a counter before immigration, or apply for the e-VoA online before flying.

phrases.registerNotes: The answer to Tujuannya apa? or Keperluannya apa? (What's the purpose of your visit?). Just Liburan. (A holiday.) is fine too.
phrases.pitfallNote: Liburan is a holiday as in a trip or time off; a public holiday is hari libur.

phrases.registerNotes: The answer to Berapa lama di Indonesia? (How long are you in Indonesia?). Swap the time: sepuluh hari (ten days), satu bulan (a month).
phrases.pitfallNote: No word for 'for' is needed before a length of time. Selama (for, during) is fine but optional.

phrases.registerNotes: The answer to Menginap di mana? (Where are you staying?). Have your hotel's name and address ready, as the arrival forms ask for it too.
phrases.pitfallNote: Menginap is staying the night somewhere; tinggal is living there.

phrases.registerNotes: Officers may ask Tiket pulangnya ada? (Do you have a return ticket?), meaning proof that you'll leave. Have it ready on your phone.

phrases.indonesian: Tempat ambil bagasi di mana, ya?
phrases.registerNotes: Signs say Pengambilan Bagasi. Bagasi is your checked luggage.
While you're still waiting, it's Koper saya belum keluar (My suitcase hasn't come out yet). Take your baggage tag to the Lost and Found desk.

phrases.indonesian: Tidak ada, Pak, hanya barang pribadi.
phrases.registerNotes: The answer when a customs officer (Bea Cukai) asks whether you have anything to declare.
phrases.cultureNote: Indonesia's drug laws are among the harshest in the world, so never carry a bag or parcel for anyone else.

phrases.registerNotes: Keberangkatan is departures and kedatangan arrivals; domestik is domestic. Big airports have separate terminals, so check yours on your ticket.
Signs say Gate in English and many people say gate too, but announcements use pintu: melalui pintu tujuh (through gate seven).

phrases.english: How long is the flight delayed?
phrases.registerNotes: In everyday speech people say delay: Pesawatnya delay (The flight's delayed). Announcements say mengalami keterlambatan (is delayed).
